A day for each feast

Yalda Night

Yalda Night: Celebrating Light and Poetry

Yalda Night marks the longest night of the year with warmth, poetry, and a feast honoring the triumph of light over darkness. Gather family to share traditions, stories, and special Persian dishes that bring brightness to the season.

  1. Evening / 7:00 pm

    Opening the Sofreh with Sharbat

    Begin your Yalda Night by serving aperitif glasses of pomegranate and rosewater cordial with mint and lime to welcome guests and set a festive mood.

    Recipes: Pomegranate And Rosewater Cordial

  2. Evening / 7:30 pm

    Meze Platter and Warm Flatbread

    Lay out a meze spread featuring fresh herbs with feta and walnuts, beet yogurt dip topped with pistachios, and olives marinated in pomegranate molasses, accompanied by warm flatbread for sharing.

    Recipes: Herb Platter · Beet Yogurt Dip · Olives in Pomegranate Molasses

  3. Night / 8:30 pm

    Main Course Feast

    Serve a rich main course of walnut-pomegranate stew with duck or chicken, saffron rice cake layered with barberries and chicken, and okra stew for vegetarians, complemented by Shirazi salad and sesame-topped Barbari bread.

    Recipes: Walnut Pomegranate Stew · Saffron Rice Cake With Barberries And Chicken · Okra Stew · Shirazi Salad · Sesame-Topped Barbari Bread

  4. Night / 9:30 pm

    Dessert and Fruit

    Enjoy traditional sweets like saffron rice pudding dusted with cinnamon, alongside fresh pomegranate and watermelon fruit to refresh and delight the palate.

    Recipes: Saffron Rice Pudding · Pomegranate And Watermelon Fruit

  5. Late Night / 10:00 pm

    Ajil-e Shab-e Yalda for Good Fortune

    Share a bowl of roasted nuts and dried fruits, known as Ajil-e Shab-e Yalda, symbolizing good fortune and abundance for the coming year.

    Recipes: Roasted Nuts and Dried Fruits

  6. Late Night / 10:30 pm

    Reading Hafez Poetry and Storytelling

    Gather around the fire’s glow to read from the poet Hafez, share stories, and reflect on the promise of returning light as the night deepens.

  7. Before Dawn / 4:30 am

    Drawing Hafez Divinations

    Conclude the vigil by drawing divinations from Hafez’s poetry, offering hope and guidance as the first light of dawn breaks after the longest night.

End your Yalda Night with hearts warmed by poetry, family, and the bright promise of returning light.
